# ADR 0136: Play-Mode Graph Debug Shell and Domain Providers

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-08-17
Amends: ADR 0123
Relates to: ADR 0006, ADR 0011, ADR 0033, ADR 0082, ADR 0084, ADR 0085, ADR 0116, ADR 0135, ADR 0137

## Problem

Play mode currently gives Behavior Tree a fixed top-level debug tab alongside
Game View and Scene View. The tab is present even when no Behavior Tree runner
exists. Animation Graph execution has no equivalent source-graph runtime view,
despite the same author needing to understand live state, transitions, resolved
Animation Set bindings, and parameters.

Copying the Behavior Tree tab for every graph domain would create one top-level
tab per domain, duplicate Graph Canvas behavior, and make Behavior Tree an
accidental architectural template. That conflicts with ADR 0006: graph storage,
identity, selection, and presentation foundations are domain-neutral, while
runtime semantics remain domain-specific.

The current Behavior Tree debugger already demonstrates both sides of the
boundary. It reuses shared Graph Canvas rendering, but its live runtime meanings
(active path, Running, Success, Failure, blackboard, reset reasons) are Behavior
Tree concepts. Animation runtime meanings are different and must not be forced
into those statuses.

A second issue is source coherence. Runtime debugging must map live execution
back to stable `NodeId`/`EdgeId`, but an Editor working copy may differ from the
disk copy or from the source generation that produced the running instance.
Debug UI must detect that condition rather than silently render runtime state on
the wrong source.

## Decision

### 1. Play mode exposes one domain-neutral Graph Debug entry

The Play-mode primary views are conceptually:

```text
Game View | Scene View | Graph Debug
```

`Graph Debug` is one shell for all runtime graph domains. Behavior Tree is no
longer a permanently privileged top-level tab.

The Graph Debug entry is hidden when the current runtime world contains no
debuggable graph execution target. This is preferred over a permanently disabled
tab because the shell represents live runtime state, not a general authoring
editor, and empty chrome provides no action.

If the selected target disappears while the user is already in Graph Debug, the
open shell may remain long enough to show a concise "target no longer exists"
state and allow selection of another target. It must not continue presenting the
last snapshot as live.

### 2. The shell enumerates actual runtime graph execution targets

Providers enumerate only graph instances that exist in the current Play runtime
world. The shell groups or lists them by runtime Entity and domain, for example:

```text
Player
  Animation Graph: PlayerGraph

Enemy01
  Behavior Tree: EnemyAI

Enemy02
  Behavior Tree: EnemyAI
```

An asset existing in the project is not enough to appear. A graph is listed only
when a runtime instance/provider can observe execution for an Entity.

Selection identity is runtime-session-local plus stable authoring identity. An
ECS entity index/generation may participate in runtime lookup but MUST NOT be
persisted into project data.

### 3. Graph Debug shell owns graph-neutral interaction and presentation

The shell owns behavior that is meaningful across graph domains:

- runtime target list and selection;
- resolution of the source Graph identity;
- shared Graph Canvas presentation;
- source `NodeId` and `EdgeId` selection;
- Frame All and focus/frame-source-target commands;
- generic active/highlight overlay primitives;
- runtime Entity selection/navigation;
- details-pane hosting;
- stale-source detection and explanation;
- read-only debug mode and disabled mutation affordances where appropriate; and
- lifecycle when Play starts/stops or a target disappears.

The shell does not own Behavior Tree or Animation semantics.

Graph Canvas remains the shared canvas. Graph Debug MUST NOT fork a second
Animation-only or Behavior-Tree-only canvas implementation.

### 4. Runtime semantics are supplied by domain-specific debug providers

Each runtime graph domain integrates through an Editor-side provider/adapter.
The conceptual contract is:

```text
GraphDebugProvider
  domain identity + display label
  enumerate live runtime targets
  resolve source Graph identity
  obtain domain runtime snapshot
  map runtime source identity -> NodeId / EdgeId
  produce common highlight/focus primitives where meaningful
  provide domain-specific details/overlay presentation
  report runtime/source generation and stale-source state
```

The exact Rust trait shape is an implementation detail. The responsibility split
is normative.

Providers live at the application/Editor integration boundary. Runtime domains
expose GUI-free read-only observation DTOs; they do not depend on egui, the
Editor crate, Graph Canvas widgets, or window state.

The common shell MUST NOT require every provider to encode its semantics into one
universal status enum. Shared primitives such as "active node", "active edge",
"severity marker", or "focus this source ID" are allowed; domain-specific state
remains domain-specific.

### 5. Behavior Tree becomes the first provider, not the universal debug model

The Behavior Tree provider uses ADR 0123's real executor snapshot and exposes, as
applicable:

- active path;
- current Running node;
- Success/Failure state and recent terminal transitions;
- abort/reset reason;
- per-node elapsed time;
- blackboard values;
- recent transitions; and
- runtime/validation errors mapped to source nodes.

The existing Behavior Tree runtime semantics and `NodeId` mapping remain valid.
Only its top-level Editor presentation changes: the dedicated fixed Play tab is
replaced by the Graph Debug shell.

### 6. Animation Graph runtime debugging observes the actual controller

Animation Preview remains an authoring tool. Graph Debug observes the actual
Animation Controller running in Play.

The Animation Graph provider must expose enough read-only runtime state to answer
what animation the Entity is executing and why. The first complete contract
includes, where meaningful:

- runtime Entity;
- Animation Graph asset and `GraphId`;
- Animation Set asset;
- current State `NodeId`;
- previous and next State when a transition is active;
- transition source/destination and transition progress;
- State elapsed time and clip/playback time;
- graph parameter names and current runtime values;
- selected/resolved `MotionSlotId` and display name;
- resolved motion variant;
- resolved `MotionSource` / Animation Clip identity;
- animation-event firing history sufficient for recent diagnosis;
- active transition and the condition/reason that made it eligible/taken; and
- runtime error or unresolved binding state.

The Graph Canvas highlights the current State and active transition using source
IDs. Details show the Animation Set resolution chain so an author can move from:

```text
State
  -> MotionSlotId
  -> Animation Set binding / selected variant
  -> MotionSource
  -> concrete clip
```

without inferring the result from the rendered character alone.

Transition-reason presentation is observational. It may report evaluated
conditions/parameters or another stable runtime reason descriptor; it must not
reimplement transition evaluation in the Editor.

### 7. Animation Preview and Graph Debug have separate authority

**Animation Preview** is authoring-time simulation for inspecting clips,
transitions, graph structure, and edits without requiring a running game.

**Graph Debug** is read-only observation of the actual Play runtime controller.

Preview may use temporary authoring parameters or seek state that never exists in
the game. Graph Debug must not write those controls back to the runtime simply to
make the visualization convenient.

If Play runtime uses a source generation older than the current Editor working
copy, Graph Debug marks the source as stale. It may overlay source IDs only when
the mapping remains valid. It MUST NOT claim that the newest working copy is what
the runtime is executing.

### 8. Source resolution follows the Editor working-copy contract

ADR 0137 defines the authoritative Editor working copy.

When Graph Debug resolves source documents for navigation and canvas display, it
uses the current Editor working copy when one exists, with disk as fallback only
when no live working copy exists. Separately, the provider reports the identity
or generation used to create the running instance.

This creates an explicit comparison:

```text
runtime source identity/generation
vs.
current Editor working-copy identity/revision
```

If they differ, the shell presents stale-source state. It must not silently
reload disk and thereby hide unsaved changes, and it must not silently pretend a
new working copy produced an older running instance.

### 9. Add Node presentation is semantic, not a redundant domain heading

The shared node schema/catalog remains authoritative for available node types.
This ADR changes only palette presentation.

For the current Animation Graph schema, where the meaningful choices are
`Entry` and `State`, Add Node should present those choices directly. The string
`Animation Graph` is not useful as a category heading when every listed item is
already in that domain.

As the domain grows, categories should describe node meaning, for example:

- State;
- Blend;
- Control; and
- Utility.

A domain name may still appear in search/filter context when multiple domains
are intentionally mixed, but a single-domain palette MUST NOT require a
redundant domain heading.

Behavior Tree keeps meaningful semantic categories such as composite, decorator,
condition, and action.

### 10. Graph Debug is read-only and never becomes a second runtime controller

The shell and providers observe real runtime state. They do not own execution,
transition decisions, Behavior Tree traversal, Animation Set resolution, or
parameter mutation.

Pause/step/breakpoint or explicit runtime-edit controls may be added later, but
each write-capable debugging feature needs a separately defined runtime-control
contract. Read-only observation is the baseline.

## Scope / Non-goals

This ADR covers Play-mode graph target discovery, the shared Graph Debug shell,
domain providers, Behavior Tree integration, Animation Graph runtime debugging,
stale-source handling, and Add Node category presentation.

It does not:

- replace the existing authoring Graph editors;
- remove Animation Preview;
- force runtime semantics into the domain-neutral Graph model;
- add Visual Script runtime semantics;
- define graph serialization changes;
- make runtime debug state persistent;
- implement pause/step/breakpoints; or
- implement the described UI in this ADR-only change.

## UX model

The normal flow is:

```text
enter Play
  -> live graph targets are discovered
  -> Graph Debug appears only when at least one target exists
  -> choose Entity + graph domain
  -> source Graph opens read-only in shared canvas
  -> active source IDs are highlighted
  -> domain details explain runtime-specific state
  -> navigation may open the authored source for repair
```

When no target exists, Play keeps only its relevant non-graph primary views.

## Diagnostic ownership

Runtime/provider failures shown in Graph Debug follow ADR 0135. A provider may
supply runtime diagnostic evidence, but repairable authoring diagnostics remain
owned by Problems. Graph Debug may show a concise local state/error linked to the
relevant Problems entry or source target.

The shell does not duplicate full Problems text.

## Graph Debug architecture

The architecture is:

```text
runtime domain
  -> GUI-free execution snapshot + stable source mapping
  -> Editor domain provider
  -> common Graph Debug target model / highlight primitives
  -> shared Graph Canvas + target selector + details host
```

Future graph domains integrate by adding a provider and runtime observation DTO,
not by adding another permanent Play tab or another graph canvas.

## Domain-specific debug provider contract

A provider must define:

- a stable domain key used only for runtime-debug registration;
- a localized/display label;
- how live targets are enumerated;
- how a runtime instance resolves to a source Graph;
- which `NodeId`/`EdgeId` values are active or focusable;
- the runtime snapshot/revision identity used by stale-source detection;
- domain-specific details and optional overlay meaning; and
- how the provider behaves when source or runtime state disappears.

A provider must not:

- mutate the source Graph as a side effect of observation;
- depend on display names for source identity;
- make the runtime crate depend on Editor UI types; or
- copy a domain's semantic state into the common Graph serialization model.

## Animation Preview responsibility boundary

Animation Preview answers "what would this authored graph/clip do under preview
controls?" Graph Debug answers "what is this Play-mode controller doing now?"

The two may share Graph Canvas and source-resolution utilities. They must not
share mutable simulation state or substitute one another's snapshot as
authoritative.

## Working-copy / saved-copy model

Graph Debug consumes ADR 0137's working-copy read contract. Disk is not an
automatic freshness source.

A runtime instance may legitimately be older than the current working copy.
That is represented as a stale-source condition, not resolved by reading a
different hidden copy.

## AI Studio presentation boundary

No AI Studio presentation rule is introduced here. AI Studio local/detached
presentation is governed by ADR 0131 as amended alongside this ADR suite, and
remote access by ADR 0133.

AI Studio or future agents may inspect Graph Debug snapshots only through an
explicit read-only capability; the Graph Debug shell itself is not an authoring
writer.

## Stable ID / serialization impact

No Graph, GraphView, Scene, Animation Set, or Behavior Tree serialization changes
are introduced.

Existing `GraphId`, `NodeId`, `EdgeId`, `MotionSlotId`, Entity and Asset IDs
remain the mapping keys. Runtime target handles, execution generations, debug
history, selection, highlights, stale flags, and details-pane state are
transient.

## Public API / crate boundary impact

Runtime graph domains may need richer public read-only snapshot DTOs. Those DTOs
belong with the runtime/domain ownership that computes the semantics.

The Editor owns provider registration and Graph Debug presentation. The shared
authoring Graph foundation remains GUI/runtime-semantics neutral. Runtime crates
must not depend on `editor`.

If a common debug descriptor crate is later justified, it must contain only
GUI-free observation/source-mapping contracts and must not become a dependency
that forces Behavior Tree and Animation semantics into one type.

## Migration / compatibility

Existing Behavior Tree execution snapshots and source `NodeId` mappings remain
valid. Their UI moves from the fixed dedicated Play tab into the provider shell.

Existing Animation Preview remains available.

No project files migrate. Existing Graph node categories remain schema metadata;
only palette presentation of a redundant single-domain heading changes.

## Testing strategy

Implementation requires automated tests for:

- Graph Debug hidden when no provider enumerates a live target;
- mixed Animation/Behavior targets enumerate under the correct Entities;
- target disappearance cannot leave a stale snapshot labeled live;
- common canvas selection/frame-all works for provider source graphs;
- stable `NodeId`/`EdgeId` mappings drive highlights;
- stale working-copy/runtime generations are detected;
- Behavior Tree provider presentation matches executor snapshot state;
- Animation provider reports current State, transition, parameters, slot, set,
  resolved motion/clip, event history, and error state from runtime evidence;
- transition reasons are observed, not reevaluated in Editor code;
- Graph Debug never mutates graph documents; and
- Add Node omits the redundant Animation Graph category while keeping future
  semantic category grouping possible.

## Visual Validation requirements

This ADR-only documentation change requires no Visual Validation.

Implementation of the Play header, Graph Debug shell, runtime overlays, target
list, details pane, stale-source presentation, or Add Node palette requires
Visual Validation. Required visual scenarios include:

- Play with zero graph targets;
- Play with Animation Graph only;
- Play with Behavior Tree only;
- Play with both domains on multiple Entities;
- active Animation transition with visible progress;
- stale source state;
- long Entity/asset/slot names without clipping; and
- Add Node with the current Entry/State-only Animation Graph schema.

## Rollout / implementation phases

1. Extract the existing Behavior Tree fixed-tab integration behind a provider and
   introduce the Graph Debug shell.
2. Add live-target discovery and zero-target tab hiding.
3. Move Behavior Tree runtime presentation into the provider without changing
   executor semantics.
4. Extend Animation runtime observation DTOs and add the Animation provider.
5. Add stale working-copy/runtime source detection through ADR 0137.
6. Simplify Animation Graph Add Node presentation.
7. Add future graph domains only through the provider contract.

## Rejected alternatives

### Add a permanent Animation Graph tab beside Behavior Tree

Rejected. Every future graph domain would add another top-level tab and duplicate
shared interaction.

### Copy the Behavior Tree debugger and rename its statuses

Rejected. Running/Success/Failure/Abort are Behavior Tree semantics, not a
universal graph runtime model.

### Put every runtime semantic into one common GraphDebugStatus enum

Rejected. It would make the domain-neutral layer depend on the union of all
current and future graph semantics.

### Always show a disabled Graph Debug tab

Rejected for the baseline UX. A hidden entry when there are no live targets keeps
Play chrome relevant. An already-open shell may still explain target loss.

### Read source graphs from disk on every debug refresh

Rejected. It hides unsaved Editor working copies and can overlay runtime state on
a source the user is not actually editing.

### Use display names to map runtime nodes to source nodes

Rejected. Names are editable and non-unique; stable `NodeId`/`EdgeId` are the
mapping contract.

### Merge Animation Preview and runtime Graph Debug

Rejected. Preview simulates authoring choices; Graph Debug observes the actual
running controller. Treating them as one authority makes stale/runtime
differences impossible to explain.
